Company Law and the Myths

1) The relationship between ownership and control of companies is complex and not always clear-cut; 2) The role of shareholders has been exaggerated in the past; 3) There is no single 'best' way of organizing the ownership of companies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of shareholders in company law and the extent to which they can be said to own companies, or to be owners of companies.

the extent to which the company law model is consistent with the idea that shareholders are owners. It will be argued that the company law model of the company is not consistent with shareholder ownership and,

the extent to which the traditional model of the company, based around the primacy of shareholder rights and the separation of ownership from control, has been undermined by the rise of institutional investors.

shareholder ownership of companies is a myth.
